CHATUCHAK WEEKEND MARKET

With more than 15,000 shops and 200,000 visitors every Saturday and Sunday, Bangkok’s Chatuchak
Weekend Market is a popular place with visitors to Thailand. You can find plants, flowers, music, jewelry,
clothes, food, and even animals!

The market is a great place to find bargains, and prices are generally low. Most people bargain, but some
don’t, so don’t worry if you don’t want to bargain. Just go with a friendly smile and have enough cash in your
pocket. There are ATMs for cash, but they are difficult to find, and many vendors don’t take credit cards.
The market is huge, and many people walk in circles, even with a map. Don’t try to see it all in one day!

The market is open from 8:00 to 6:00 Saturday and Sunday. It’s good to get there early, before it gets too
busy. Wear light, comfortable clothing and bring a bottle of water. And for lunch, try some of Thailand’s
famous snacks, such as fried scorpions!

The market is very easy to get to. It’s only a five-minute walk from Mo Chit station on Bangkok's Skytrain.
Many people come by train but leave by taxi. It’s easier to get your purchases back to your hotel that way!
